w: Barely more than a stone box on a tiny islet, the Turtle Tower sits marooned in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake -- and somehow carries more symbolic weight than any skyscraper in the city. Also known as the Tortoise Tower, it's the single most recognisable piece of architecture in Hanoi, arguably in all of Vietnam.
s: A tiny tower marooned in the middle of Sword Lake
_facts: Small tower in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake (Sword Lake)
Also called the Tortoise Tower
One of the most iconic and recognisable pieces of architecture representing Hanoi and Vietnam

w: Raised at the end of the 19th century near the old Ham Long street it borrowed its name from, this Catholic church -- officially dedicated to St Anthony of Padua -- ranks alongside Cua Bac Church and St Joseph's Cathedral as one of Hanoi's three major churches.
s: One of Hanoi's three major Catholic churches
_facts: Roman Catholic church in Hoan Kiem district, central Hanoi
Built end of the 19th century near the old Ham Long street
Officially the Church of St Anthony of Padua
One of the three major churches of Hanoi, with Cua Bac Church and Saint Joseph Cathedral

w: Ho Chi Minh read Vietnam's Declaration of Independence from this spot in Ba Dinh Square on 2 September 1945. His embalmed body now lies inside the granite mausoleum built after his death in 1969 -- open to the public most mornings, closed Mondays and Fridays, and still a genuine site of pilgrimage.
s: The granite resting place of Vietnam's founding leader
_facts: Mausoleum holding the body of Ho Chi Minh in central Ba Dinh Square
Site where Ho read the Declaration of Independence on 2 September 1945, founding the Democratic Republic of Vietnam
Ho was Chairman of the Workers' Party of Vietnam from 1951 until his death in 1969
Open to the public every morning except Monday and Friday

w: Hanoi's 12-hectare centrepiece carries its legend in the name: Hoan Kiem translates as 'Lake of the Returned Sword.' It answered to other names too -- Luc Thuy, 'Green Water Lake,' and Thuy Quan, 'Mariner's Lake' -- but today it's simply the fixed point every walk through the old quarter circles back to.
s: The 'Lake of the Returned Sword' at Hanoi's centre
_facts: Freshwater lake of about 12 hectares in the historical centre of Hanoi
Name means 'Lake of the Returned Sword' or 'Lake of the Restored Sword'
Also known as Sword Lake (Ho Guom) or Ta Vong Lake
Formerly named Luc Thuy Lake ('Green Water Lake') or Thuy Quan Lake ('Mariner's Lake')
One of the major scenic spots in the city and a focal point for public life

w: Before 1954 this was the Palace of the Governor-General of Indochina -- French colonial power's seat in Vietnam. It has kept its function under new management: now the official residence of Vietnam's president, though the real paperwork happens next door at the Tonkin Palace, which houses the presidential office.
s: The Governor-General's palace, now the president's
_facts: Located in Hanoi
Official residence of the president of Vietnam and seat of the presidential office
Before 1954 named the Palace of the Governor-General of Indochina
Now used for state ceremonial activities, while the Tonkin Palace houses the Office of the President

w: Named for the Ba Dinh Uprising, an anti-French revolt of 1886-87 fought under the Can Vuong banner, this square became the stage for a bigger declaration: Ho Chi Minh's reading of Vietnam's independence here on 2 September 1945. His granite mausoleum went up on the same ground after his death, and pilgrims still come.
s: Where Ho Chi Minh declared Vietnam's independence
_facts: Square in Hanoi where Ho Chi Minh read the Proclamation of Independence on 2 September 1945
Named after the Ba Dinh Uprising, an anti-French rebellion of 1886-87, part of the Can Vuong movement
The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was built here after his death
Remains a major site of tourism and pilgrimage

w: Founded by colonial decree in 1917 as the central library of Indochina, this institution has worn four names in four decades -- Pierre Pasquier, Bibliotheque Nationale, Bibliotheque Centrale de Hanoi -- before settling on its current title in 1958. It opened to the public in 1919, a very French idea of the archive.
s: Indochina's central library, renamed four times over
_facts: Established by decree of 29 November 1917 as the central library of Indochina
Opened to the public in September 1919
Took successive names: Pierre Pasquier (1935), Bibliotheque Nationale (1945), Bibliotheque Centrale de Hanoi (1947)
Given its present name on 21 November 1958
